name: Context menu
purpose: Offer the actions for the item under the pointer, using the familiar right-click, long-press and menu key conventions.
whenToUse: Rows, cards, files, tabs or canvas objects that have several actions (rename, duplicate, share, delete).
Power users who expect right click, as an accelerator for actions that are also reachable elsewhere.
Touch: the same menu on long press (550ms).
An overflow (more) button menu that lists the same actions.
whenNotToUse: As the only way to reach an action. Every action must also be reachable without right click (toolbar, overflow button, keyboard).
Menus with more than about 10 items. Group them, or move rarely used items elsewhere.
Replacing the browser menu on text, links or inputs where the native menu is what users expect.
Nested submenus more than one level deep.
A single action. Show the button directly.
anatomy: Surface: neutral glass (--s4 at 88%), --r-lg, 4px padding, shadow.
Item: 30px minimum height (40px on touch), optional 15px leading icon, label, optional right aligned shortcut.
Heading (optional): small muted caps label above a group, same left edge as items.
Check mark: neutral (--text) on the right for toggled items.
Danger item: --danger text and icon, last, after a separator. No tinted fill.

variants.description: Opens at the pointer position and flips to stay inside the viewport.
Opens below an overflow (more) button, aligned to its end.
variants.useWhen: The visible alternative to right click.

variants.description: Items with a trailing check mark (menuitemcheckbox).
variants.useWhen: Toggling a view option or a favourite.

behavior: Open: contextmenu event (right click, Shift+F10, Menu key) and a 550ms long press on touch.
Focus moves to the first enabled item on open and returns to the opener on close.
Keys: Up and Down move and wrap, Home and End jump, Enter or Space activates, Esc closes, Tab closes.
Type-ahead: typing letters moves to the next item whose label starts with them (600ms buffer).
Group related items with separators; order: common actions first, danger last after a separator.
Shortcuts are right aligned and muted; they are hints, the menu does not bind them.
Closes on selection, outside click, scroll or resize.
Disabled items stay visible but muted when their state is informative; otherwise leave them out.
accessibility: role=menu with role=menuitem (or menuitemcheckbox with aria-checked) items; label the menu with aria-label.
Roving tabindex: only the active item is tabbable; arrow keys move focus.
Opening and closing restore focus to the opener.
Shift+F10 and the Menu key open the menu for the focused item so keyboard users are not excluded.
Danger meaning is carried by the label and icon, not by colour alone.

Item text is --text on the glass surface (9.9:1 on --s4). Shortcut hints use --text-2 (4.8:1 on --s4), so they stay readable, and are hidden on touch devices where keyboard shortcuts do not apply. If a hint is not worth reading, do not show it. Danger items use --danger (4.55:1 on --s4) together with an icon and a clear verb, and sit last after a separator.
